items.subject: accountancy
items.body: A firm’s profit after retaining ₹15,000 in reserve is ₹75,000. Its tangible assets are ₹10,00,000 and outside liabilities are ₹3,00,000. Goodwill under capitalisation of average profit is ₹50,000. What is the normal rate of return?

source_excerpts.quote: Capitalisation of Average Profits: Under this method, the value of goodwill is ascertained by deducting the actual firm’s capital in the business from the capitalized value of the average profits on the basis of normal rate of return. This involves the following steps: (i) Ascertain the average profits based on the past few years’ performance. (ii) Capitalize the average profits on the basis of the normal rate of return to ascertain the capitalised value of average profits as follows: Average Profits × 100/Normal Rate of Return (iii) Ascertain the actual firm’s capital (net assets) by deducting outside liabilities from the total assets (excluding goodwill and ficticious assets). Firms’ Capital = Total Assets (excluding goodwill) – Outside Liabilities Where outside Liabilities include both long term and short term Liabilities. (iv) Compute the value of goodwill by deducting net assets from the capitalised value of average profits, i.e. (ii) – (iii

items.subject: english
items.body: According to paragraph 1, what do smartphone notifications do to the people in the room?

options.text: Repeatedly draw their attention away from conversations
Help them listen more closely to others
Make their time pass more slowly
Prevent them from looking at screens

items.passage_text:
(1) A room is filled with people whose faces glow in the light of their smartphones. Moments drift away like autumn leaves in the wind. Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

(2) When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

(3) Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

(5) The writer urges readers to value presence and engagement in moments that matter. What defines people is the depth of their connections and the richness of their experiences, rather than their number of likes or followers.

source_excerpts.quote: Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

(1) A room is filled with people whose faces glow in the light of their smartphones. Moments drift away like autumn leaves in the wind. Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

(2) When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

(3) Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

(5) The writer urges readers to value presence and engagement in moments that matter. What defines people is the depth of their connections and the richness of their experiences, rather than their number of likes or followers.
